toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The cancellations are mainly caused by the Quillbook accounting sync, not the price rise. Quillbook accounts churned at about 6% a month after April, whether or not they had a price change (repriced 6.2%, Founders locked 5.9%). Repriced accounts with no accounting connector barely moved (1.8% to 1.9%), so the April increase alone does not explain the rise. Quillbook's v2 retirement on 30 March caused invoices to go missing or duplicate; 34% of affected accounts cancelled, against 8% of unaffected ones. Tallymarsh shows only a small change within normal noise, though its error log has not been reviewed. Seasonality and the mobile release do not fit the data.

Confidence is good on the Quillbook link and on rejecting the price explanation. It is weaker on Tallymarsh and on the slow-support link, which may be a result of the sync problems rather than a cause.

Next steps: move the Quillbook fix to top priority and contact affected accounts to correct invoices. Do not switch off the duplicate-invoice hold, since it is preventing duplicates. Do not reverse the price rise yet; it would cost about $220k a month without addressing the cause. Review the Tallymarsh logs before committing to a rebuild.
